title: Adaptive smoke-window with explainable failure tags and deferred-retry CI policy
author: Sanjay Mehra
description:
Motivation: Our existing smoke-eval CI uses a fixed time/window and simplistic pass/fail semantics which causes two problems: (1) transient infra flakiness and model nondeterminism create noisy failures; (2) failures surface without contextual signals, making triage slow. This PR implements an adaptive smoke-window controller plus explainable failure tags and a deferred-retry policy so CI can (a) surface higher-fidelity regression signals, (b) reduce noisy interrupts, and (c) provide actionable failure metadata for triage.

Summary of changes: introduce an adaptive sliding window sampler and score aggregator that expands/contracts the smoke cohort based on recent variance and historical stability; add failure tagging that attaches explainable failure categories (e.g. tokenization-mismatch, prompt-truncation, latency-spike, model-regression, sample-variance) to CI failures; implement a deferred-retry policy with backoff and priority-based re-run (hot-path regressions are re-run earlier); expose runtime metrics and tagging to CI artifacts and to the observability endpoint.

Files changed (high level): added eval_harness/ci/smoke_controller.py, eval_harness/ci/failure_tagger.py, ci/configs/smoke_profiles.yml, tests/eval_harness/test_smoke_controller.py, tests/eval_harness/test_failure_tagger.py, docs/ci/guide-adaptive-smoke.md, scripts/ci/upload-smoke-artifacts.py.

Design notes: the smoke_controller uses a two-tier algorithm: (1) a short-window variance detector to decide whether to widen the sample window (more samples) when instability exceeds a threshold; (2) a long-window dampening to avoid oscillation. Thresholds are surfaced as config profiles per service in smoke_profiles.yml. Failure_tagger applies a rules+classifier hybrid: deterministic rules first (timeouts, tokenization errors) then a lightweight model for semantic mismatches; tags are appended to the CI artifact JSON so downstream triage UIs can surface suggested owners and remediation playbooks.

Rollout plan: gated feature flag (ci.adaptive_smoke_enabled) default off; enable in canary CI for eval-harness repo for 48h, compare signal-to-noise ratio and alert counts vs baseline. If successful, flip on for other repos behind an org-level feature flag and a Linear rollout task.

Testing and validation: unit tests added for controller heuristics and tagger rules; synthetic stability harness used to assert expected widening/contracting behavior; integrated end-to-end smoke run in a temporary CI job (see CI artifact links in pipeline). Performance: controller adds minimal latency to scheduler (~2-8ms per batch) and memory overhead is negligible.

Backward compatibility: default behavior when feature flag is off is identical to prior smoke runner. Configs are additive and old profiles remain valid.

Checklist: [x] design review, [x] unit tests, [x] integration smoke job, [x] docs update, [x] feature flag gating, [x] observability metrics emitted.

Related: Linear ENG-1724 (reduce CI noise / smarter smoke runner), ENG-1820 (triage tooling for eval regressions), SUP-914 (customer-reported noisy alerts).
commits_summary: 3 commits: 1) smoke controller + config and initial tests; 2) failure tagger + classifier and tag mapping; 3) CI integration, docs, and observability plumbing. See commits: 'controller: add adaptive smoke window', 'tagger: failure tagging rules + classifier', 'ci: emit smoke artifacts and add feature flag'.
review_threads: Elena: 'Can you sketch how the long-window dampening avoids thrash when model updates roll through?' — Author: 'Added comments and unit tests demonstrating dampening with simulated model-step changes; long window defaults to 72h and uses exponential smoothing to avoid flip-flop.'; Tomas: 'Failure tags look promising; how do we avoid false positives from classifier?' — Author: 'Classifier is only consulted after rule checks and requires confidence>0.85 to tag; lower-confidence examples are sent to 'needs-human' tag for triage.'; Priya: 'Make sure observability uses existing metric names' — Author: 'Mapped new metrics to eval.harness.* namespace and added a migration shim in metrics export.'; Approvals: Elena approved after requested doc clarifications were addressed; Tomas approved after classifier threshold was parameterized; Priya approved after CI artifact schema validated.
ci_logs_summary: Initial CI run: lint passed, unit tests had two flaky failures (fixed by increasing test timeout), integration job failed on artifact upload (credentials issue) — re-run after fix succeeded. Final CI: all checks passing. Artifacts: smoke-artifact-20260220.json uploaded.
release_notes: Introduce an adaptive smoke-window controller and explainable failure tagging for smoke CI to reduce noisy alerts and improve triage. Feature guarded behind ci.adaptive_smoke_enabled. No customer-facing API changes.
notes_for_oncall: If noise increases after rollout, toggle ci.adaptive_smoke_enabled=false for the affected org and collect the smoke artifacts (eval_artifact.json) for analysis. Failure tags are in artifact key 'failure_tags'.
